figures.title: One fp32 number: 1 sign, 8 exponent, 23 mantissa
figures.caption: fp32 spends 1 sign bit, 8 exponent bits, and 23 mantissa bits. fp16 spends 1 + 5 + 10, bf16 1 + 8 + 7, e4m3 1 + 4 + 3, and e5m2 1 + 5 + 2. The exponent sets range: fp16 tops out at 65,504, bf16 at 3.39 × 10^38, e4m3 at 448, and e5m2 at 57,344. The mantissa sets resolution near 1.0, where the gap is 2^−23 ≈ 1.19 × 10^−7 in fp32, 2^−10 ≈ 9.8 × 10^−4 in fp16, and 2^−7 = 0.0078125 in bf16.
figures.alt: A horizontal bar split into three fields labelled sign, exponent, and mantissa, with widths 1, 8, and 23 bits. The exponent field is shaded and outlined in the accent; the bit count is printed under each field, and the bar runs from most significant on the left to least significant on the right. The caption gives the corresponding splits for fp16, bf16, e4m3, and e5m2, their largest finite values, and the gap between representable values near 1.0.

anim.intro: Press Play or Next to spend one fp32 number bit by bit.

steps.label: One sign bit: the value is (-1)^sign x 2^(exponent - bias) x (1 + mantissa).
Eight exponent bits, with the mantissa held fixed, set the range: fp16 tops out at 1.9990234375 x 2^15 = 65,504 and its smallest normal is 2^-14, about 6.1 x 10^-5.

Twenty-three mantissa bits set the resolution. Near 1.0 the gap is 2^-23, about 1.19 x 10^-7, so 1 + 2^-8 = 1.00390625 lands exactly. fp16's ten bits give a gap of 2^-10, roughly 9.8 x 10^-4; bf16's seven bits give 2^-7 = 0.0078125, half a gap above 1.0, so round-to-nearest-even returns 1.0 and the 0.00390625 vanishes.

figures.title: Mixed precision: fp32 state and reductions, low-precision matmuls
figures.caption: A mixed-precision step keeps master weights, optimizer state, gradient accumulation, the loss and its scale, softmax, layer norm, batch norm, reductions, and post-unscale gradient clipping in fp32. Matrix multiplies go low precision: bf16, or e4m3 for the fp8 forward pass and e5m2 for the fp8 backward pass. fp8's range is small, so each cast needs a per-tensor scale: 448/amax for e4m3 and 57,344/amax for e5m2. The multiply still accumulates in fp32.
figures.alt: Two aligned panels. The left, fp32 state and reductions, lists master weights, optimizer state, gradient accumulation, the loss and its scale, softmax, layer norm, batch norm, reductions, and gradient clipping after unscaling, all in fp32. The right, low-precision matmuls, lists the forward matrix multiply in e4m3 for fp8 or bf16, the backward matrix multiply in e5m2 for fp8 or bf16, the fp8 weight and activation casts, and the per-tensor scales 448/amax for e4m3 and 57,344/amax for e5m2. A note on the left gives the gap at 1.0 as 1.19 × 10^−7 in fp32 against 9.8 × 10^−4 in fp16 and 0.0078125 in bf16.

panels.title: fp32: state and reductions
panels.note: The update 1.0 + 1 × 10^−5 needs fp32: the gap at 1.0 is 1.19 × 10^−7 in fp32, 9.8 × 10^−4 in fp16, 0.0078125 in bf16.

panels.title: low-precision matmuls
panels.note: Only the casts and the multiply inputs are low precision; the accumulation stays fp32.

anim.intro: Press Play or Next to follow one mixed-precision step and see what stays in fp32.

steps.label: The fp32 master copy holds the weights and optimizer state. The update 1.0 + 1 x 10^-5 needs it: the gap at 1.0 is 1.19 x 10^-7 in fp32, but 9.8 x 10^-4 in fp16 and 0.0078125 in bf16, so in either narrow format the weight would round back to 1.0 and freeze.

Cast weights and activations to e4m3 for the forward matmul, or stay in bf16. The e4m3 scale is 448/amax, so a tensor whose largest absolute value is 12.0 is multiplied by 448/12.0 = 37.333 before the cast.

Cast gradients to e5m2 for the backward matmul, or stay in bf16. The e5m2 scale is 57,344/amax: a gradient tensor peaking at 0.5 is multiplied by 57,344/0.5 = 114,688 and divided back after the matmul.

Only the casts and the multiply inputs are low precision: the accumulation stays in fp32, along with softmax, layer norm, batch norm, the loss, and reductions. An e4m3 significand is four bits, so the product of two needs up to eight and is exact.
Unscale the gradients, clip after unscaling because clipping a scaled gradient changes the threshold, and apply the fp32 update to the master copy.

sources.note: Micikevicius et al., Mixed Precision Training (ICLR 2018): fp32 master weights, loss scaling, and fp16 compute.
Micikevicius et al., FP8 Formats for Deep Learning: e4m3 and e5m2 field widths, largest finite values, and per-tensor scaling.
Kalamkar et al., A Study of BFLOAT16 for Deep Learning Training: bf16 keeps fp32's exponent range and spends the mantissa.
